before.html:
Question 1
?

Let a=⟨−2,−1,−4⟩ and b=⟨6,−5,3⟩. Find the vector projection of a onto b.

a
⟨−5735,1914,−5735⟩
b
⟨−5770,1914,−5770⟩
c
⟨−5735,1914,−5770⟩
d
⟨−5735,1935,−5735⟩
e
⟨0,0,0⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: The projection is (a·b)/(b·b) times b. Since a·b = -12+5-12 = -19 and b·b = 36+25+9 = 70, the projection is (-19/70)⟨6,-5,3⟩ = ⟨-57/35,19/14,-57/70⟩.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Let $a=⟨-2,-1,-4⟩$ and $b=⟨6,-5,3⟩.$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
after.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{(-2)\cdot 6+(-1)\cdot (-5)+(-4)\cdot 3}{{6}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{3}^{2}}b \\  & =-\frac{19}{70}⟨6,-5,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{57}{35},\frac{19}{14},-\frac{57}{70}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating a Vector Projection Using Components
content.problem: Let $a=⟨-2,-1,-4⟩$ and $b=⟨6,-5,3⟩.$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
content.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{(-2)\cdot 6+(-1)\cdot (-5)+(-4)\cdot 3}{{6}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{3}^{2}}b \\  & =-\frac{19}{70}⟨6,-5,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{57}{35},\frac{19}{14},-\frac{57}{70}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Let r=⟨−5,1,3⟩ and s=⟨n,−2,4⟩. Given that the projection of r onto s is the zero vector, find the value of n.
n=
Submit

decision.explanation: Since s is nonzero, its projection of r is zero exactly when r·s = 0. Thus -5n-2+12 = 0, so -5n+10 = 0 and n = 2.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
Since $r$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $s$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
r⊥s\,⟹\,r\cdot s=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot s & ={r}_{x}\cdot {s}_{x}+{r}_{y}\cdot {s}_{y}+{r}_{z}\cdot {s}_{z} \\  & =(-5)\cdot n+1\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 4 \\  & =-5n-2+12 \\  & =10-5n.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot s & =0 \\ 10-5n & =0 \\ n & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?
Let a=ti+4j−k and b=2i−j. Given that the projection of a onto b is the zero vector, find the value of t.
t=
Submit

decision.explanation: Since b is nonzero, the projection is zero exactly when a·b = 0. With a = ⟨t,4,-1⟩ and b = ⟨2,-1,0⟩, this gives 2t-4 = 0, so t = 2.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular.

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =t\cdot 2+4\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot 0 \\  & =2t-4+0 \\  & =2t-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 2t-4 & =0 \\ 2t & =4 \\ t & =2 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

t=

EXPLANATION

Since a is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector b equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular.

So, we must have a⊥b⟹a⋅b=0.

Computing the dot product, we obtain a⋅b=ax⋅bx+ay⋅by+az⋅bz=t⋅2+4⋅(−1)+(−1)⋅0=2t−4+0=2t−4.

Setting the dot product equal to 0, we get a⋅b=02t−4=02t=4t=2t=2.
